name: 333. Perplexity chat usage: search context size and per-tool counts, the streamed final frame matches, errors carry error_type (perplexity search usage)
description: TXE-6549, contract C5, C10, C6. Local fixture regression, no live provider calls: run with providerErrorFixture=1 against the gateway of tests/e2e/api/provider_config/provider-error-fixture.config.json, whose perplexity entry points at tests/e2e/api/runners/provider-error-fixture.mjs. The fixture answers /chat/completions for sonar-search-usage with Perplexity's own usage shape: search_context_size (the tier of the per-request search fee), top-level citation_tokens and num_search_queries, a flat cost, and tool_calls_details.<tool>.invocation; streamed, every frame carries a usage and the frame with the finish reason carries the full one. Before TXE-6549 the non-streamed usage had no search_context_size and no per-tool counts, and the stream used the generic OpenAI decode, which has no place for the top-level counts, so the final frame lost num_search_queries, citation_tokens and tool_usage. Rows 1-3 pin the chat routes (non-streamed, streamed, streamed on the OpenAI-compatible route), rows 4-5 the Responses route, which serves Sonar models from chat. Rows 6-7 pin C6: sonar-invalid-model gets Perplexity's 400, whose error.code is a number; the status is kept, streamed or not, and the error carries extra_fields.error_type caller_invalid_request. Perplexity's native /v1/responses (non-Sonar models) is not reached by this change.

item.name: 333.1 perplexity /v1/chat/completions non-streamed perplexity/sonar-search-usage usage carries search_context_size, per-tool counts, citation tokens and cost (perplexity search usage)

exec: pm.test('the token counts are the vendor\'s', function () {

pm.expect(usage && { prompt: usage.prompt_tokens, completion: usage.completion_tokens, total: usage.total_tokens }, 'usage: ' + JSON.stringify(usage)).to.eql({ prompt: 12, completion: 40, total: 52 });
pm.test('search_context_size is the tier the vendor billed', function () {
pm.test('tool_usage carries the search count and every tool\'s call count', function () {
pm.expect(usage && usage.tool_usage, 'usage: ' + JSON.stringify(usage)).to.eql({ web_search: { num_requests: 3 }, per_tool: { web_search: { num_requests: 3 }, fetch_url: { num_requests: 1 } } });
pm.test('citation tokens, search queries and reasoning tokens are kept', function () {
pm.expect({ citation: d.citation_tokens, searches: d.num_search_queries, reasoning: d.reasoning_tokens }, 'usage: ' + JSON.stringify(usage)).to.eql({ citation: 300, searches: 3, reasoning: 8 });
pm.test('the vendor\'s cost is kept', function () {
// The OpenAI-compatible routes send cost as a bare number, the native routes as an object.
pm.expect(typeof cost === 'number' ? cost : cost && cost.total_cost, 'usage: ' + JSON.stringify(usage)).to.equal(0.03026);
